item.title: Iran walks away from US peace talks as Zarif floats deal
item.description: Mohammad Javad Zarif, the former Iranian foreign minister who helped negotiate the 2015 nuclear deal, has published a detailed peace proposal in Foreign Affairs urging Tehran to "declare victory" and strike a comprehensive agreement with the United States to end the ongoing war. The essay, published late Thursday, drew swift pushback from Gulf diplomats and comes amid deep market skepticism that a ceasefire is near.

item.title: Iran says it 'never refused' Pakistan-hosted talks with US
item.description:
Pakistan's Foreign Office on Saturday denied reports that its bid to broker talks between the United States and Iran had collapsed, even as Tehran has yet to signal willingness to engage in formal negotiations despite weeks of diplomatic pressure from Islamabad and Beijing.

The denial came a day after Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar spoke by phone with Saudi counterpart Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud to discuss a five-point peace initiative that Pakistan and China jointly unveiled on March 31. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, meanwhile, said Saturday that his country "never refused to go to Islamabad," pushing back on Wall Street Journal reporting that Tehran had formally notified mediators it would not send officials to Pakistan for talks.

item.title: Vietnam's growth slows as Middle East war fuels Asian energy crisis
item.description: The widening conflict in the Middle East is generating cascading economic shockwaves across Asia and Africa, straining fuel supplies, weakening currencies, and forcing governments into emergency crisis mode as they scramble to shield households and businesses from surging energy costs.

item.title: Surcharges hit global commerce as Hormuz crisis deepens
item.description: More than five weeks after U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran triggered the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the cascading effects on global supply chains continue to deepen. Jet fuel prices have surged past $195 per barrel, container shipping costs have jumped 40 to 60 percent on major trade lanes, and carriers from airlines to parcel services are passing the pain to businesses and consumers through a wave of surcharges.

item.title: Iran claims downing 160-plus drones, multiple US jets
item.description: Iran's top air defense commander declared on Saturday that the country's forces have destroyed more than 160 enemy drones and downed several advanced fighter jets since the start of the US-Israeli military campaign, which began on February 28. Brigadier General Alireza Elhami, commander of the Khatam al-Anbiya Joint Air Defense Headquarters, said the results were achieved using domestically developed methods and equipment capable of targeting even fifth-generation stealth aircraft — claims that, if verified, would mark a notable shift in the balance of modern aerial warfare.

item.title: Analyst raises Nvidia target to $220 amid $1T order pipeline
item.description:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told a crowd of more than 30,000 at the company's annual GTC developer conference in San Jose on March 16 that the chipmaker now has visibility of more than $1 trillion in orders for its Blackwell and Vera Rubin AI chip platforms through the end of 2027. The figure doubles the $500 billion demand estimate Huang had cited just months earlier, reflecting what he called an "inflection point" in AI inference computing.

The disclosure caps a breakout fiscal year for Nvidia. The company reported record revenue of $215.9 billion for fiscal 2026, ended January 25, up 65% from the prior year, according to its earnings release. Fourth-quarter revenue reached $68.1 billion, a 73% year-over-year increase.

item.title: Interception debris strikes Oracle building in Dubai amid Iran conflict
item.description:
Debris from an aerial interception struck the facade of Oracle's building in Dubai Internet City on Saturday morning, according to the Dubai Media Office, in the latest incident highlighting the risks to civilian infrastructure from the ongoing conflict between Iran, the United States, and Israel.

No injuries were reported. "Authorities confirm that they responded to a minor incident caused by debris from an aerial interception that fell on the facade of the Oracle building in Dubai Internet City," the Dubai Media Office wrote on X. The incident was quickly contained, officials said.

item.title: Tanzania's rice surplus hits record as East Africa faces historic drought
item.description: Tanzania's paddy rice production reached 2.6 million tonnes in the 2024/2025 season, far exceeding domestic consumption needs and generating a surplus that could prove critical for a region grappling with drought and rising food costs. The bumper harvest comes as nearly 26 million people across Somalia, Ethiopia, and Kenya face extreme hunger driven by failed rains, and as global food prices climb amid the ongoing Middle East conflict.

item.title: Five EU nations push windfall tax on energy firms amid oil surge
item.description: From travel bans in West Africa to fuel tax cuts in South Africa and a push for windfall taxes in Europe, governments are deploying an array of emergency measures to cushion the economic blow of oil prices that have surged past $100 a barrel amid the ongoing conflict in Iran.

item.title: IRGC strikes Israel-linked ship in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on Saturday targeted a container ship it identified as linked to Israeli interests, setting the vessel on fire in a drone attack in the Strait of Hormuz, according to multiple reports. The strike on the vessel — referred to as MCS Ishika by Iran's WANA news agency — was part of the 95th wave of Operation True Promise 4, the sprawling retaliatory campaign Iran has waged since the U.S.-Israeli coalition struck Iran on February 28.

item.title: Pakistan reverses record fuel hike as Asia reels from Iran war energy crisis
item.description: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, triggered by the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran that began on February 28, is sending shockwaves through import-dependent economies across Asia and the developing world. From the Philippines to Pakistan to Vietnam, governments are scrambling to contain fuel shortages, record price spikes, and currency crises that threaten to derail economic growth across the region.

item.title: U.S. Dollar Index hits highest level since May 2025
item.description: The US Dollar Index climbed to its highest level since May 2025, crossing the 100.08 mark on April 3, 2026, as a confluence of geopolitical turmoil and shifting Federal Reserve expectations drove investors into the greenback. The rally marks a sharp reversal from late 2025, when the index languished in the mid-90s, and is now reshaping currency markets worldwide.

item.title: China pushes five-point peace plan as Iran war nears fifth week
item.description: As the US-Israeli war against Iran enters its fifth week with no end in sight, China has emerged as the most active diplomatic player pushing for a ceasefire, while the conflict's disruption of global energy supplies sends shockwaves through economies from Manila to Seoul.

item.title: Global services sector contracts for first time in 3 years amid Iran war oil shock
item.description: A month into the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, the economic consequences are cascading across the globe. Maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has collapsed by 95%, according to a United Nations Conference on Trade and Development report released on April 2, choking off roughly a fifth of the world's oil supply and sending energy prices surging. The S&P Global Services PMI fell to 49.8 in March 2026, slipping below the 50.0 threshold that separates expansion from contraction for the first time in more than three years.

item.title: Iran's radar-silent missile systems down US jets, exposing electronic warfare gap
item.description: Iran's downing of a U.S. F-15E Strike Eagle and strike on an A-10 Thunderbolt on Friday marked the first loss of manned American aircraft to enemy fire during Operation Epic Fury, exposing what analysts say is a critical vulnerability in U.S. electronic warfare: the inability to counter heat-seeking, radar-silent air defense systems.

item.title: Bangladesh, Thailand impose emergency measures as energy crisis deepens
item.description: Bangladesh and Thailand are rolling out emergency measures to combat a worsening energy crisis fueled by conflict in the Middle East, with Dhaka slashing work hours and Bangkok confronting warnings of construction industry collapse as diesel prices nearly triple on global markets.

item.title: US burns through critical weapons stockpiles five weeks into Iran war
item.description: Five weeks into Operation Epic Fury, the United States and Israel have unleashed devastating firepower on Iran, striking more than 11,000 targets and claiming a 90% reduction in Tehran's missile and drone attacks. Yet Iran's low-cost, high-disruption approach to the conflict has exposed a stark vulnerability in Western military doctrine: expensive, precision-guided weapons systems are being consumed at unsustainable rates to counter cheap, mass-produced threats.

item.title: UAE intercepts 79 Iranian projectiles as strikes batter Gulf infrastructure
item.description:
The UAE Ministry of Defence said on Saturday that its air defense systems intercepted 23 ballistic missiles and 56 drones launched from Iran on April 4, marking another day of sustained aerial bombardment against the Gulf state. The latest wave brings the total number of projectiles engaged since the conflict began on February 28 to 498 ballistic missiles, 23 cruise missiles, and 2,141 drones.

The attacks, which began after coordinated U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February, have inflicted mounting damage on the UAE's energy and industrial infrastructure, raising questions about the long-term economic toll even as air defenses continue to neutralize the vast majority of incoming threats.

item.title: Zelensky meets Erdogan in Istanbul for ceasefire talks
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Istanbul on Saturday for security talks with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, with discussions centered on ceasefire efforts and the broader diplomatic push known as the Istanbul Process. The meeting at the Dolmabahçe Palace comes at a sensitive moment, just one day after Erdogan held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

item.title: IRGC claims strikes on U.S. Patriot system, bases in 95th attack wave
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced on Friday that its forces struck U.S. military positions on Bubiyan Island in Kuwait and a Patriot air defense system in northern Bahrain as part of the 95th wave of its Operation True Promise 4 campaign, marking the latest escalation in a war now entering its sixth week.
